pairs.question: Quid agis hic?
pairs.derivation: Phanostrata asks Lampadio what he is doing here; he answers 'something to make you glad.' Speaker labels PHAN./LAMP. and the inline verse number 545 stripped. Both are short complete utterances; no trimming needed.

pairs.question: Quid id est?
pairs.answer: Hinc ex hisce aedibus paulo prius vidi exeuntem mulierem.
pairs.derivation: Phanostrata asks what it is; Lampadio answers that he saw a woman coming out of this house. Answer ends at the first full stop, before Phanostrata's next question 'Illam quae...?'. Speaker labels and verse numbers stripped.

pairs.question: Men, mulier, vocas?
pairs.derivation: Lampadio asks Melaenis whether she is calling him; she answers 'You.' Speaker labels MEL./LAMP. stripped. Both complete utterances.

pairs.question: Quis istic habitat?
pairs.derivation: Melaenis asks who lives there; Lampadio answers 'Demipho, my master.' Speaker labels stripped; line 599 begins this exchange.

pairs.question: Nempe istic est, qui Alcesimarcho filiam suam despondit in divitias maxumas?
pairs.derivation: Melaenis asks whether that is the man who betrothed his daughter to Alcesimarchus into great wealth; Lampadio confirms 'That's the very man.' Verse number 600 stripped from mid-line; the question runs across the line break verbatim and contiguous.

pairs.question: iam scis?
pairs.derivation: Lampadio asks Melaenis whether she now understands; she answers 'I grasp that well enough.' Drawn from the close of Lampadio's speech (line 613); only the interrogative 'iam scis?' is kept as the question. Verse numbers and speaker label stripped.

pairs.question: aut quis es?
pairs.answer: Ego sum illius mater, quae haec gestitavit.
pairs.derivation: Halisca's line is 'Quid istuc negoti est? aut quis es?'; the operative interrogative answered is 'quis es' ('who are you?'), to which Phanostrata replies 'I am the mother of her who wore these.' Answer ends at the full stop before Halisca's next question. Verse number 745 stripped from mid-line.

pairs.question: Hicine tu ergo habitas?
pairs.derivation: Halisca asks whether Phanostrata lives here; Phanostrata answers 'You're divining (i.e. you've guessed right).' A genuine affirmative reply. Speaker labels stripped.

pairs.question: ubi ea est, quae gestitavit?
pairs.derivation: Phanostrata (after 'Mulier, perge dicere.') asks where the girl who wore the tokens is; Halisca answers 'Here, next door.' Only the interrogative sentence kept as the question. Speaker labels and verse numbers stripped.

pairs.question: quot annos nata dicitur?
pairs.derivation: Phanostrata asks how many years old the girl is said to be; Halisca answers 'Seventeen.' The preceding 'Ne obloquere rusus. perge porro dicere.' is framing addressed to Lampadio and is omitted; the interrogative is kept. Editorial brackets and verse number stripped.

pairs.question: sed quid est nomen tuae dominae?
pairs.derivation: Phanostrata asks the name of Halisca's mistress; Halisca answers 'Melaenis.' Editorial brackets around <est> stripped (words kept). The question spans the line break (tuae / dominae) verbatim and contiguous; speaker labels and verse numbers removed.

pairs.question: Ere, unde is?
pairs.derivation: Lampadio asks Demipho where he is coming from; Demipho answers 'From the senate.' Speaker labels and inline verse number stripped; both complete utterances.
